name: Damaged Building Detection Dataset
description: Rapid damage assessment is of crucial importance to emergency responders during hurricane events, however, the evaluation process is often slow, labor-intensive, costly, and error-prone. New advances in computer vision and remote sensing open possibilities to observe the Earth at a different scale. However, substantial pre-processing work is still required in order to apply state-of-the-art methodology for emergency response. To enable the comparison of methods for automatic detection of damaged buildings from post-hurricane remote sensing imagery taken from both airborne and satellite sensors, this paper presents the development of benchmark datasets from publicly available data. The major contributions of this work include (1) a scalable framework for creating benchmark datasets of hurricane-damaged buildings and (2) public sharing of the resulting benchmark datasets for Greater Houston area after Hurricane Harvey in 2017. reputation: A useful remote-sensing benchmark for disaster response research, but it is relatively specialized and not as widely adopted as mainstream vision benchmarks.
notes: Non-LLM, domain-specific benchmark based on post-hurricane aerial and satellite imagery; dataset size and label quality can vary by split and preprocessing.
